survivors_flagged.one_line: The $1.52B Long Ridge sale to MARA has regulatory approval and is expected to close by the end of Nov-2026. It removes $1.16B of asset debt and pays down about $300M of parent debt (around $25-30M a year in interest saved). The deal was known since Q1 and the stock trades ~$3.5, so the setup is mid-arc; check the Series B preferred and the USD deal.

verified.catalyst: MARA's ~$1.52B purchase of Long Ridge has regulatory approval and should close by end-Nov-2026. It removes about $1.16B of Long Ridge debt and repays about $300M of parent debt. The $255M USD Group terminal purchase also closes in Nov-2026.
verified.dated_milestone: Long Ridge close expected by 2026-11-30 (per the Q3 release of 2026-11-05). Next date: the closing 8-K, then Q4/FY results around late Feb 2027, which should show the first post-sale balance sheet.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 yes: named buyer, MARA Holdings. G2 yes: signed sale agreement dated 2026-04-30, regulatory approval received, closing dated end-Nov. G3 no: the debt paydown figures have been public since Q1/Q2, and closing does not create an unpriced equity figure.
verified.edge: L. The event is real and close, but the common gains little from it. Run-up: from the pre-deal base of $5.67 (2026-04-29) to $3.79 today is -33%, so the deal itself was sold off. The approval/Q3 leg did run: $2.94 on 2026-11-05 to $3.79, +29% in two weeks, peaking at $4.38 on 11-11. Remaining: about 0-15% to a provenance-checked SoP midpoint of roughly $4, with a range of $0 to $6 depending on the EBITDA multiple. The capital structure does not support a large re-rating.
verified.primary_source: FIP 8-K Ex.99.1 Q3 2026 earnings release (2026-11-05, accession 0001899883-26-000042): balance sheet at 2026-09-30; Long Ridge regulatory approval, close by end-Nov. FIP/MARA deal press releases (2026-04-30). FMP EOD prices 2026-04-20 to 2026-11-19 (close $3.79 on 2026-11-19).
verified.analysis: Numerator re-derived from the 2026-09-30 balance sheet (8-K Ex.99.1). Consolidated debt is about $2.83B; about $1.53B of it is held-for-sale Long Ridge debt. After the deal and the $300M paydown, roughly $1.0B of debt should remain. Ahead of the common also sit the RailCo Series A pref at $1.4B redemption (carried $1.04B, accreting about $34M a quarter) and the Series B convertible pref at $192M redemption (carried $155M). Claims senior to the common total about $2.6B, plus about $255M more for the USD purchase. Remaining EBITDA is about $218M ex-Long Ridge annualized, plus about $58M from USD: roughly $275M. At 10-12x that is $2.75-3.3B of EV, so common equity comes out at about $0 to $0.7B, or $0 to $6 a share, against a $448M market cap (118.2M shares). The midpoint is about where the stock trades. Scoring the equity, not the event (capped at 4, scored 3). Closing de-risks the balance sheet, but at redemption value the pref stack takes most of the remaining value. The upside depends on the Series A redemption/refinancing and on rail and terminal growth, not on this closing. Gaps: the 10-Q was not read, so the Series A PIK/accrual terms, the exact Long Ridge net proceeds, and the RailCo pref covenants on proceeds are unverified. Accrued unpaid RailCo pref dividends of about $121M were reported secondhand.
